question: If \(\log_8 3=p\) and \(\log_3 5=q,\) then, in terms of \(p\) and \(q,\) \(\log_{10}5\) equals
solution:
The relations \(8=2^3\) and \(10=2\cdot5\) suggest rewriting the logarithms in base \(2\). By the change-of-base formula,
\[
p=\frac{\log_2 3}{\log_2 8}
=\frac{\log_2 3}{3},
\]
so \(\log_2 3=3p\). Similarly,
\[
q=\frac{\log_2 5}{\log_2 3}
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\log_2 5=q\log_2 3=3pq.
\]
The product rule now relates the requested base \(10\) to the known quantities:
\[
\log_2 10=\log_2 2+\log_2 5=1+3pq.
\]
All bases used are greater than \(1\), and \(1+3pq=\log_2 10>0\), so the final denominator is nonzero. Changing base once more gives
\[
\log_{10}5
=\frac{\log_2 5}{\log_2 10}
=\frac{3pq}{1+3pq}.
\]
The answer is \(\frac{3pq}{1+3pq}\), choice D.
